conflict_topics: Whether alcohol should be present at the housewarming
Location/storage of alcohol (fridge, cooler, outside landing)
Shared-hosting responsibilities and who can block party elements
Compensation/refund for purchased drinks and precedent for future events
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents provide concrete reasons (religious prohibition, ownership, hosting responsibilities) rather than only tone.
Multiple practical compromises proposed: cooler box, keeping drinks on the landing, alcohol-free party, refund offer.
Conversation is realistic and goal-oriented (need to decide before guests arrive), with occasional positional restatement (A on tenancy rights; D on religious prohibition).
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive agreement was reached by the end of the transcript. Practical solutions (cooler, placing drinks on the landing, refund offers) were proposed (Agent B/C suggested a cooler or landing; Agent D offered to pay back the purchase), but Agent D repeatedly stated that the issue is principled: 'it's not okay to have alcohol in the house' (Turn 6) and 'it still feels like we're hosting a party with alcohol' (Turn 25). Agent A rejected the compromises and asserted majority/tenancy rights: 'So there is no compromise then. It's either your way, or nothing. Three of us live here too.' (Turn 26). Because neither side accepted the other's position and no mutually accepted concrete arrangement was spoken by all affected parties, the dispute remained unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent D consistently maintained a principled objection to alcohol being in the house and did not concede (Turn 6, Turn 25).

Agent A consistently defended the right to host and to have purchased drinks, resisted compromises that would limit future planning, and rejected proposed compromises by the end (Turn 7, Turn 22, Turn 26).
Agents B and C shifted toward compromise-oriented proposals (cooler, landing placement) attempting to reduce material conflict but did not secure acceptance from the primary disagreeing parties.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'Is there a problem?' Agent C: 'Is it about it being in the fridge with the food?' No substantive disagreement was yet expressed.

Agent D: '...I'm not comfortable with having alcohol at our housewarming.' Agent A: 'We all agreed to the party last week. Why is this an issue now?' Clear, substantive disagreement about whether alcohol should be present at the event.

Agent D: '...because I'm Muslim, it's not okay to have alcohol in the house.' Agent A: 'We all live here. ... I'm not asking you to drink it.' Religious prohibition vs. shared-flat hosting rights articulated, raising the normative stakes.

Agent B: 'What if we get a cooler box for the drinks?...not in the fridge with everyone's food.' Agent C: 'A cooler box is a good idea. That solves the fridge issue.' A partial practical alternative was proposed (addresses storage) but the core dispute (alcohol in the house) remained unsettled.

Agent D: '...the problem isn't just the fridge, it's having alcohol in the house for the party at all.' Agent A: 'It's not just your house, Agent D. It's a shared flat.' Cooler suggestion rejected; core incompatibility reasserted.

Agent D: 'As one of the hosts, I can't be part of a party that serves alcohol in my own home.' Agent A: 'So don't be a host. The rest of us are still having the party.' Conflict sharpens around hosting responsibilities and whether one resident can block alcohol.

Agent B: 'We all live here. We're all hosts.' Agent A: 'She just said she can't be a host. So what are we meant to do?' Positions remain opposed; disagreement over shared-hosting obligations continues.
Agent B and Agent C emphasize urgency: 'We have to figure something out... It'll be a disaster if we're arguing when [guests] are here.' Pressure to resolve but no settlement or change in positions.

Agent D: 'What if we just make it alcohol-free?...make some mocktails.' Agent A: 'And what am I supposed to do with all the drinks I've already bought?' A concrete accommodation (alcohol-free party) proposed, but Agent A resists on ownership and prior purchase grounds.

Agent D: 'I can pay you back for them.' Agent A: 'It's not just about the money. What happens next time? Are we all supposed to plan everything around what one person is or isn't comfortable with?' A raises systemic/precedent concern, re-elevating the disagreement beyond this single event.

Agent B: 'What if we keep the drinks in a cooler, but we put it just outside the front door? On the landing?...' Agent C: 'That could work. It's not in the house then.' A new practical compromise addresses location, but Agent D has not accepted it yet.

Agent D: '...it still feels like we're hosting a party with alcohol.' Agent A: 'So there is no compromise then. It's either your way, or nothing. Three of us live here too.' Positions hardened; A frames majority/tenancy rights and rejects compromise, D maintains principled objection.

substantive_insights: The core tension is normative: a resident's religious prohibition against alcohol in the shared living space versus other residents' expectation to host events including alcohol.

Practical fixes (moving drinks, using a cooler, refunding purchases) address physical placement and ownership but do not resolve the symbolic or normative objection to alcohol being present in the home.
Agent A raises a precedent problem: accommodation of one person's religious practice could create future constraints on what the household can plan collectively.
